{"items":["MEMO — Northstar Wellness, April 8
From: Lena Ortiz, Studio Manager
The Tuesday evening strength class averaged 18 attendees, up from 13 in March. Members especially liked the shorter circuit stations and coach Devon’s form checks. We had two minor issues: one loose resistance-band clip and a crowded check-in area around 5:45 p.m. Facilities will replace the clip, and I’ll ask reception to open the side desk during peak arrival times. Date: May 2
Attendees: Priya Shah, Marcus Bell, Jo Kim
We reviewed April member feedback. The most common request was for beginner-friendly lunchtime sessions, particularly mobility and basic dumbbell training. Jo will collect attendance and feedback for four weeks. No equipment purchases are needed for the pilot.","SHORT REPORT — Greenline Health Club
Prepared by: Noel Grant
Our six-week walking challenge ended Friday with 47 participants completing at least 20 logged walks. The group recorded a combined 612 miles, though several entries were submitted late. Participants mentioned improved energy and better consistency when walking with a partner. For the next round, we should add optional stretching prompts and a simple weather-related rescheduling rule. The prize drawing will include three fictional gift cards from local café partner Bright Bean.","INTERNAL NOTE — Apex Motion
The front desk received three questions this week about whether members should exercise while recovering from a cold. Staff used the approved guidance: pause intense training when symptoms are significant, return gradually, and consult a healthcare professional when symptoms are severe or persistent. We should print a small reminder for the lobby rather than relying on verbal explanations. Tessa will draft language by Friday, keeping it general and avoiding medical claims.","STAFF MEMO — Willow Peak Pilates
Our Saturday morning reformer schedule is now consistently full, with 11 of 12 spots booked on average. Instructor Amara noted that first-time clients need more time learning spring settings, so she recommends opening the room 10 minutes earlier. The cleaning checklist is being completed, but the spray bottles are often left empty after the second class. Please refill them before closing and initial the supply log. We’ll review the schedule again after two more weekends.","PROJECT UPDATE — VitalArc Mobile Coaching
The nutrition habit tracker is ready for a limited test with eight volunteer clients. Current features include meal-timing notes, water reminders, and a weekly reflection prompt. We intentionally excluded calorie targets from this version to keep the tool focused on practical habits and avoid presenting individualized medical advice. Early testers found the reminder language too formal. Sam will revise it to sound more conversational before Tuesday’s check-in.","MEETING SUMMARY — Redwood Recovery Center
The team discussed adding a low-intensity Sunday session for members returning to exercise after a break. Coach Elliot proposed a 40-minute format: breathing, gentle mobility, supported balance work, and an optional cool-down walk. Staff agreed that the class description should clearly state that participants may stop at any time. We also need a simple registration question about previous exercise experience. The first trial is planned for June 16, pending room availability.","INTERNAL REPORT — Blue Finch Fitness
Attendance for the early-morning cycling block increased from 9 riders in January to 15 in February, then leveled at 14 in March. Feedback suggests the playlist and consistent start time are helping. Two riders asked for a slightly longer warm-up, while one prefers less sprint work. Coaches will test a four-minute gradual warm-up next week and offer a reduced-intensity option during intervals. No injuries or equipment failures were reported during the period.","OPERATIONS NOTE — Cedar & Stone Wellness
The new foam rollers and yoga mats arrived on Monday. Inventory shows 24 mats, 16 long rollers, and 10 shorter rollers. All items were labeled with the studio name before being placed in storage. Please remind clients not to leave equipment in the hallway, as it blocks the emergency access route. We are also changing the closing routine so the final instructor checks the storage shelves and records any damaged items before leaving.","CLIENT PROGRAM REVIEW — Silver Meadow Coaching
Jordan Lee completed the first month of the beginner movement program with strong consistency: three scheduled sessions each week and two optional walks. Jordan reported less stiffness after work and said the shorter sessions felt manageable. The next phase will keep the same frequency while adding light balance exercises and one rest-day planning prompt. We’ll continue emphasizing gradual progress, comfortable effort, and communication with a qualified professional if pain or unusual symptoms appear."]}

{"items":["Mara Velez, a street photographer from Portland, has started carrying a tiny thermal printer on weekend walks. She photographs interesting doors, prints the images immediately, and leaves a copy in the mailbox or doorway when owners are home. “It turns the camera into a conversation starter,” she said. Mara has made about 60 prints since January, and several residents have invited her inside to document old family porches before they are renovated.","The fictional camera maker Northstar Imaging announced its new Lumen 8 mirrorless model on Tuesday. The $1,299 camera includes a 33-megapixel sensor, improved low-light autofocus, and a quieter mechanical shutter. Local photographer Ian Cho tested a preproduction unit during a rainy concert and liked its handling. He said the biggest surprise was the battery life, which lasted through nearly 1,100 photographs despite heavy use of the electronic viewfinder.","A small exhibition called “Laundry Day” opened this week at the Bellweather Arts Center in Dayton. Photographer Priya Nand spent two years photographing laundromats after midnight, focusing on people waiting beside spinning machines. The images are bright, funny, and occasionally lonely. Priya said she chose the subject because laundromats gave her “a reason to be out with a camera without planning anything.” The show includes 28 prints and runs through October 19.","After losing a hard drive containing several years of photographs, travel blogger Evan Rusk has changed his backup routine completely. He now keeps working files on two portable drives and uploads finished projects to an encrypted cloud archive. Evan admitted he used to postpone backups because they felt boring. “That mistake cost me more than the cameras,” he said. His new checklist takes five minutes after each trip, and he has already persuaded three friends to copy the system.","The Harbor City Photography Club is offering free portrait sessions for residents over 70 next month. Volunteers will use a borrowed studio at the old ferry terminal, with appointments lasting about 30 minutes. Organizer Celia Morin said the project began after members realized many older neighbors had no recent photographs of themselves. Participants can choose a digital file or a printed 8-by-10 portrait. The club expects to photograph roughly 90 people during the four-day event.","Wildlife photographer Tomas Bell spent six months testing silent shutters while documenting foxes near a restored wetland outside Millhaven. He said the quieter setup helped him work closer without disturbing the animals, although it created occasional rolling-shutter distortions when foxes sprinted across the frame. Tomas plans to publish a small book in spring, with proceeds supporting the wetland trust. His favorite image shows a fox carrying a yellow rubber duck from a nearby children’s picnic area.","A new photo-sharing app called FrameNest is drawing attention for limiting public feeds to 25 images per person. Founder Lila Hart said the restriction was inspired by old contact sheets, where photographers had to edit carefully before showing their work. Users can still upload unlimited private albums, but only selected images appear on their profiles. Early tester Noah Kim likes the slower pace. He said the app has led to more useful comments and fewer endless scrolling sessions.","Photographer Benji Ortiz has turned an abandoned supermarket into an unusual camera obscura. He covered the windows with thick black fabric and left a small lens opening in the entrance wall, projecting the surrounding neighborhood upside down across the empty aisles. Visitors can walk through the dim space and watch buses and pedestrians drift over the shelves. Benji said the installation took three weekends and cost less than $400 using recycled materials.","A minor controversy at the Westbridge Photo Fair ended with organizers changing their image-labeling rules. Several visitors noticed that AI-assisted photographs were displayed beside conventional photographs without explanation. Festival director June Alder apologized and said future exhibits will identify editing methods, including generative tools, compositing, and extensive retouching. Photographer Malik Dean welcomed the decision. “The technology is interesting,” he said, “but people deserve to know what they’re looking at.” New labels will appear next year.","Freelance photographer Rosa Ellery has launched a monthly workshop for parents who want better family photographs without buying expensive equipment. Her first class, held in a community garden, covered window light, autofocus settings, and how to photograph children without constantly asking them to pose. Eight people attended, using phones and cameras ranging from ten-year-old compact models to professional mirrorless bodies. Rosa said the most popular tip was simply to get lower and wait for a real moment."]}

Subject: Utility accruals required for year-end reporting

Please submit estimated December utility expenses for all managed properties by January 3. Accruals should include electricity, water, waste removal, and common-area heating where applicable. Estimates must be based on the latest available invoices or usage trends and should identify any material unusual items. The current preliminary schedule contains unsupported accruals of $12,650 for three properties. The external auditors have circulated a draft management representation letter for the year ended December 31. Unless significant changes are identified, the final letter will be scheduled for signature by the chief financial officer on February 14."]}

{"items":["Energy Bills Set to Rise as Northbridge Utility Updates Tariffs

Northbridge Utility Services will increase residential electricity tariffs by 6.4% from 1 April 2027. The company said the adjustment reflects higher wholesale procurement and network maintenance costs. A typical household using 850 kilowatt-hours annually is expected to pay approximately £78 more per year. Customers on fixed-term plans will remain on their existing rates until renewal. The supplier has advised customers experiencing difficulty paying to contact its support team before missing an instalment.","Clearwater Energy Introduces Flexible Billing Options for Small Businesses

Clearwater Energy has launched a revised billing programme for small commercial customers, offering monthly, quarterly and usage-smoothing payment schedules. The initiative is intended to reduce seasonal volatility for retailers, offices and workshops. Participating businesses will receive estimated bills only when meter data is unavailable, with corrections applied after verified readings are received. Clearwater stated that customers can change payment frequency without an administrative fee, subject to account review and contract terms.","Households Encouraged to Submit Meter Readings Before Annual Review

Meridian Power and Gas is asking customers to submit electricity and gas meter readings by 30 September ahead of its annual account reconciliation. Providing current readings may help ensure that bills reflect actual consumption rather than projections. The company has published instructions for conventional, smart and prepayment meters on its customer portal. Meridian also confirmed that customers who identify a suspected billing error can request a review without suspending their normal payment arrangement.","Regulator Approves Revised Billing Standards for Regional Suppliers

The Eastborough Utilities Commission has approved updated billing standards covering statement design, payment notices and complaint handling. From January, suppliers operating in the region must display unit rates, standing charges and consumption periods in a consistent format. Commissioner Helen Ward said the changes would make bills easier to compare across providers. Falcon Grid Energy confirmed that it will update digital and paper statements before the compliance deadline and provide advance notice of any account-system changes.","Suncrest Power Reports Lower Average Bills Following Efficiency Programme

Suncrest Power reported that participating households reduced average winter electricity costs by 11% after completing its home-efficiency programme. The programme provided insulation assessments, heating controls and tailored consumption reports to 4,800 customers. Suncrest stated that the reported savings vary according to property type, occupancy and weather conditions. Customers can request an assessment through the company website, although installation support remains subject to eligibility criteria and available funding.","Billing System Upgrade Planned by Halcyon Energy Network

Halcyon Energy Network will migrate residential accounts to a new billing platform during the weekend of 12–13 February. Customers may experience delayed online statement access while account balances and payment histories are transferred. The company said direct debits will continue automatically and no action is required from customers unless bank details have changed. A dedicated helpline will operate from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. throughout the migration period to address payment or account-access concerns.","Evergreen Utilities Announces Support Credit for Eligible Customers

Evergreen Utilities has introduced a one-time £45 account credit for qualifying customers facing short-term financial pressure. Eligibility includes households receiving specified income-related benefits or referred by an approved community organisation. The credit will be applied directly to the electricity account and cannot be exchanged for cash. Evergreen stated that customers should apply by 31 December and continue making agreed payments while applications are assessed. Independent advice is available through local consumer-support services.","Corporate Energy Costs Reviewed as Larkspur Manufacturing Expands

Larkspur Manufacturing has completed a review of its energy expenditure following the opening of a second production facility in Westmere. The company expects annual electricity consumption to increase by approximately 3.2 gigawatt-hours. Under a new agreement with Beacon Commercial Energy, rates will be reviewed quarterly against market conditions, while network charges will be billed separately. Finance Director Martin Cole said the arrangement provides greater visibility over operating costs and supports the company’s emissions-reduction targets.","Pinecrest Gas and Electric Clarifies Estimated Billing Policy

Pinecrest Gas and Electric has issued a customer notice explaining when estimated bills may be generated. Estimates are used when a meter reading is unavailable, inaccessible or considered inconsistent with recent consumption. Customers can submit a reading through the mobile application, website or automated telephone service. Pinecrest said revised bills will be issued when validated data is received, and any resulting credit or balance will appear on the next statement. The company recommends submitting readings before tariff changes take effect.","Rivermark Energy Publishes Winter Payment Guidance

Rivermark Energy has published guidance for customers preparing for higher winter consumption. The supplier recommends reviewing payment amounts, checking heating schedules and confirming that account contact details are current. Customers using smart meters can access daily consumption information through the online dashboard, while other customers may request a quarterly usage summary. Rivermark warned that payment plans should be agreed before arrears accumulate and said trained advisers are available to discuss affordable repayment arrangements."]}

{"items":["Subject: A Gentle Start for Luna’s New Diet

Customer (Maya): Hello, PawPost team! My nine-year-old beagle, Luna, has been gaining weight despite eating the recommended portions. Could you suggest a healthier routine?
Agent (Elliot): Hi Maya! We’re happy to help. Please confirm Luna’s current food, daily treats, activity level, and any medical conditions. Weight changes can have several causes, so her veterinarian should rule out thyroid or joint concerns before a diet change. Meanwhile, measure meals with a cup, limit treats to 10% of daily calories, and add short, gentle walks if approved.
Customer: Thank you—I’ll schedule a checkup and start tracking meals.","Subject: Newsletter Note: Keeping Milo Comfortable in Summer

Customer (Jon): Our golden retriever, Milo, loves the park, but he’s been panting heavily after only fifteen minutes. Is this normal?
Agent (Priya): Hi Jon! Panting helps dogs cool themselves, but heavy or prolonged panting can signal overheating. Visit early or late, carry fresh water, and provide shaded breaks every 10 minutes. Avoid hot pavement—if you can’t hold your hand on it for five seconds, it’s too warm for paws. If Milo becomes weak, confused, vomits, or has bright-red gums, move him to a cool area and contact an emergency veterinarian immediately.
Customer: That’s very helpful. We’ll switch to sunrise walks.","Customer: Hi, I adopted a six-month-old kitten named Peaches from BrightTail Rescue. She hides whenever guests arrive and rarely plays while visitors are here. How can we help her feel safer?
Agent: Congratulations on Peaches! Give her a quiet room with food, water, a litter box, and hiding places. Ask guests to sit calmly and avoid reaching toward her. You can offer high-value treats or interactive toys without forcing contact. Short, positive visits are best, and she should always have an escape route. If she stops eating, hides constantly, or shows other concerning changes, consult your veterinarian.
Customer: We’ll create a guest-free retreat and let her set the pace.","Subject: Fresh Tips for a Healthier Smile

Customer (Rafael): My miniature poodle, Coco, is four years old and has noticeably bad breath. She eats normally and seems energetic. Should I be worried?
Agent (Nina): Hello Rafael! Persistent bad breath often comes from dental plaque or gum disease, even when a pet seems well. Please arrange a veterinary dental examination, especially if you notice red gums, loose teeth, drooling, or difficulty chewing. At home, use toothpaste made for dogs—never human toothpaste—and introduce brushing gradually. Dental chews may help, but they shouldn’t replace professional care or daily brushing.
Customer: Understood. I’ll ask our clinic about a dental check and safe brushing routine.","Customer: I ordered a calming supplement from FurryNest for my twelve-pound cat, Willow. The label mentions one chew daily, but our veterinarian prescribed another medication. Can Willow take both?
Agent (Sam): Thanks for checking before combining them. We can’t confirm safety without the supplement ingredients and Willow’s medication details. Please send photos of both labels to your veterinarian or pharmacist. Some calming products contain herbs that may cause sedation or interact with prescriptions. Until your clinic approves the combination, do not give the supplement. If Willow accidentally receives both and seems extremely sleepy, unsteady, or has breathing changes, seek urgent veterinary advice.
Customer: I appreciate the caution. I’ll contact the clinic today.","Subject: Travel Bulletin: A Smoother Ride for Archie

Customer (Leah): We’re driving six hours with our terrier, Archie, next month. He drools and whines during car trips. What can make the journey easier?
Agent (Derek): Hi Leah! Start with brief practice rides that end somewhere pleasant. Secure Archie in a crash-tested harness or carrier, and never let him ride loose or travel in the front seat. Avoid a large meal immediately before departure, but keep water available. Plan breaks every two hours for toileting and gentle movement. Ask your veterinarian whether motion-sickness or anxiety medication is appropriate; don’t use human medication without professional guidance.
Customer: Great checklist—we’ll begin practice rides this weekend.","Customer (Nora): My rabbit, Button, has stopped eating his usual pellets but is still nibbling hay. He seems quieter than normal. Is it okay to watch him overnight?
Agent (Omar): Hello Nora. A reduced appetite and unusual quietness can become serious quickly in rabbits because gastrointestinal problems may progress rapidly. Please contact a rabbit-experienced veterinarian today rather than waiting overnight. Keep fresh hay and water available, and avoid force-feeding or giving medication unless a professional instructs you. Note when Button last ate, drank, and passed droppings. If he becomes very weak, bloated, or stops producing droppings, seek emergency care immediately.
Customer: Thank you. I’m calling the clinic now.","Subject: Paws & Play Monthly: Safe Exercise for Senior Dogs

Customer (Evan): Our twelve-year-old lab, Harper, still wants to chase balls, but she limps afterward. How should we adjust her exercise?
Agent (Talia): Hi Evan! Please schedule a veterinary evaluation, since limping may reflect arthritis, an injury, or another condition. Until Harper is examined, replace long ball-chasing sessions with short, controlled walks on softer surfaces. Warm up slowly, avoid jumping and sharp turns, and stop if she limps during activity. Keep her lean and provide a comfortable, non-slip resting area. Your veterinarian may recommend physical therapy, joint support, or pain management tailored to her needs.
Customer: We’ll pause fetch and arrange an appointment.","Customer: My parakeet, Kiwi, has started pulling out feathers around the chest. The cage is clean, and I changed his food two weeks ago. Could boredom be the cause?
Agent (Mei): Feather picking can result from boredom, skin irritation, nutritional issues, stress, infection, or other medical problems, so an avian veterinarian should examine Kiwi. Please don’t assume it is behavioral. Keep his routine stable, provide safe toys and supervised out-of-cage time, and avoid scented sprays, smoke, and nonstick cookware fumes near him. Record when the picking occurs and bring the food packaging to the appointment.
Customer: We’ll arrange an avian visit and remove scented products from the room.","Subject: Welcome Home Guide for a Newly Adopted Dog

Customer (Sofia): We brought home a three-year-old mixed-breed dog named Jasper from KindHarbor yesterday. He won’t use the bathroom outside and has had two indoor accidents. Are we doing something wrong?
Agent (Caleb): Congratulations on Jasper’s adoption! A new environment can be overwhelming. Take him outside on a predictable schedule—after waking, eating, playing, and every few hours—and praise him immediately after he goes. Supervise closely indoors, clean accidents with an enzymatic product, and never punish him. If he strains, urinates frequently, has blood in his urine, or cannot urinate, contact a veterinarian promptly. Most newly adopted dogs improve with patience and consistency.
Customer: Thank you. We’ll establish a routine and celebrate outdoor successes."]}

{"items":["MEMO — Northstar Performance Lab
Date: 14 March 2026
Subject: Submaximal treadmill screening

Client A. Mercer completed the Bruce submaximal protocol without adverse symptoms. Resting heart rate was 62 bpm; peak observed heart rate reached 154 bpm at 10.2 METs. Blood pressure response remained within expected limits, increasing from 118/74 to 168/78 mmHg. Mild right-calf tightness was reported during recovery. Recommend calf mobility work, hydration monitoring, and repeat screening in six weeks. Clearance for moderate aerobic training is supported, pending physician review of the reported tightness.","Meeting Notes — Vela Health Systems
Participants: Dr. Imani Cole, Marcus Reed, Sofia Lin
Topic: Wearable-data validation

The team reviewed 28 days of heart-rate and step-count data from 46 enrolled participants. Optical heart-rate readings showed a mean absolute error of 3.8 bpm during steady cycling but 11.6 bpm during interval transitions. Step counts were within 6% of the reference accelerometer for walking speeds above 2.5 km/h. Action items: recalibrate interval detection, exclude device-removal periods exceeding 20 minutes, and document firmware version 4.7.2 in all future exports.","SHORT REPORT — Everwell Occupational Fitness
Assessment group: Riverton Municipal Utilities

Twenty-four employees completed a six-week conditioning program consisting of two supervised resistance sessions and one low-intensity aerobic session weekly. Mean sit-to-stand performance improved from 18 to 23 repetitions in 30 seconds. Average waist circumference decreased by 2.1 cm, while body mass changed by 0.8 kg. Four participants reported transient delayed-onset muscle soreness during week two; no injuries were recorded. Attendance was 87%. The next cycle should add individualized load progression and a brief nutrition-literacy module.","INTERNAL NOTE — Harborline Cardiac Wellness
Patient ID: HW-1842

During the 22 April supervised exercise session, the participant completed 24 minutes of recumbent cycling at an average workload of 55 watts. Heart rate remained between 88 and 103 bpm, with perceived exertion rated 11–12 on the Borg scale. The participant denied chest discomfort, unusual dyspnea, dizziness, or palpitations. Blood pressure at five-minute recovery was 126/76 mmHg. Continue current intensity for three sessions, then increase duration by three minutes if pre-exercise screening remains unremarkable.","PROJECT UPDATE — Kinetic Orchard Labs
Project: Sleep and recovery dashboard

The prototype now calculates a seven-day training-readiness index using resting heart rate, sleep duration, sleep regularity, and subjective fatigue. In pilot testing with 19 recreational runners, the index correctly identified 12 of 15 self-reported high-fatigue days. False-positive alerts occurred primarily after late evening strength sessions. Engineering will revise the algorithm to distinguish acute post-exercise heart-rate elevation from sustained morning elevation. No clinical claims should appear in the user interface until validation and compliance review are complete.","Case Conference Notes — Meridian Sports Medicine
Date: 3 June 2026

Patient: fictional case, J. Holloway, 34, recreational tennis player. Primary complaint is anterior knee pain during stair descent and deep flexion. Strength testing identified a 14% deficit in left hip abduction compared with the right side. No joint-line tenderness or instability was observed. The group recommended reducing high-volume lunges for two weeks, adding isometric quadriceps work, and progressing hip-strength exercises from band resistance to cable loading. Reassessment is scheduled after four supervised sessions.","OPERATIONS MEMO — PulseForge Training Centers
Subject: Emergency-response drill findings

The quarterly drill at the Westbridge facility lasted 17 minutes and simulated exertional collapse near the free-weight area. Staff initiated the response within 42 seconds, retrieved the automated external defibrillator in 68 seconds, and completed the handoff script without omissions. The main deficiency was incomplete documentation of witness statements. Beginning next month, managers will assign a recorder before each class and verify AED battery and pad expiration dates on the first business day.","Research Log — LumenStep Mobility Study
Entry date: 9 August 2026

Participant LS-031 completed baseline and week-four gait assessments. Comfortable walking speed increased from 1.06 to 1.18 m/s, while cadence rose from 104 to 109 steps per minute. Dual-task walking speed remained unchanged at 0.72 m/s. The participant reported improved confidence on uneven ground but continued to use a railing on stairs. Data quality was acceptable; two force-plate trials were discarded because of premature foot placement. Repeat dual-task testing is planned at week eight.","STAFF BRIEFING — Acadia Nutrition and Fitness
Topic: Protein-intake counseling protocol

Coaches should avoid prescribing a single protein target without considering body mass, kidney history, total energy intake, and client preference. For generally healthy adults engaged in resistance training, the education handout may present a broad range of 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day, subject to clinician or dietitian review when medical conditions are reported. Staff must distinguish nutrition education from individualized medical advice. All client questions involving renal disease, pregnancy, unexplained weight loss, or gastrointestinal symptoms require referral.","Quality Review Note — SummitTrack Wellness Platform
Release candidate: 2.9.0

Automated review identified three issues affecting the exercise-library metadata. The overhead-press entry listed an incorrect primary movement pattern, the rowing-machine video lacked an accessibility transcript, and two recovery timers displayed seconds as decimal minutes. The defects were reproduced in staging and assigned to Engineering. Product will delay release until metadata validation passes on iOS and Android builds. Clinical content remains unchanged, but the medical-disclaimer language should be rechecked after the timer fix."]}

{"items":["Northstar Cloud cuts deployment time with regional templates

{"items":["At Northbridge Analytics, all hiring decisions must be based on documented qualifications, role-related competencies, and business requirements. Follow-up questions are permitted only when they clarify a candidate’s experience or response. Panelists must record factual observations promptly after each interview and may not alter another panelist’s ratings. Final recommendations require documented evidence linked to the published job criteria and approval from the designated department leader.","Crestline Health Technologies requires recruiters to provide candidates with accurate information about duties, location, working hours, compensation range, and anticipated selection stages. Employees must not promise employment, guaranteed promotion, or specific benefits unless authorized in writing.
